sections.html:
High Desert country east of the Cascades is where Redmond sits, in Deschutes County at about 3,012 feet and roughly 17 miles north of Bend, the county seat. Portland is 146 miles away, Salem 129 and Eugene 126.

The city has grown fast. The estimated population was 38,547 on July 1, 2025, up from 33,274 in 2020 and 26,215 in 2010. Most of that growth came after 1990, so a large share of the housing is fairly recent, and the original townsite holds the older stock. Under many lots lies volcanic rock, a reminder that the Horse Lava Tube System reaches into town at the Redmond Caves.

sections.h2: Sun, freezes and a dry-climate house
sections.html:
The climate is dry steppe, with only about 8 to 10 inches of precipitation a year, sunny days and cool nights. Summer highs usually run from 75 to 100 degrees, winter highs often sit between 10 and 40, and the record low is minus 28. What wears on a house here is sun, big temperature swings and hard winter freezes.

  • Roofing and exterior paint take heavy sun.
  • Pipes, hose bibs and exposed plumbing face hard freezes.
  • Wood decks and fences dry out and crack over the years.
  • Landscaping needs irrigation, so a working sprinkler system helps a buyer's impression.

Fire access has come up locally. At a city council hearing in May 2025 on a new subdivision, a nearby resident pointed out that the area had only one good way out in a fire and that the neighborhood sits close to the urban growth boundary. Buyers may raise the same questions, so be ready to talk about exits, defensible space around the house and what your insurer requires.

Roberts Field is the city-run airport and the only commercial passenger airport in Central Oregon. Alaska, American, Delta and United fly there, and passenger traffic reached 1,317,665 in 2025. A $180 million expansion began in 2025 with federal help. The airport brings jobs and out-of-town buyers, while houses under the flight paths may hear aircraft.

U.S. Route 97 runs north and south through the city on the Redmond Parkway alignment that opened in 2008. Oregon Route 126 meets it and heads west toward Eugene and east to Prineville.

The city council approves new subdivisions under its Redmond 2050 Comprehensive Plan. One recent approval is Antelope Flats, a 32-home subdivision in southwest Redmond, where groundbreaking was expected six months to a year after approval and construction would take about two years. New supply close to you can compete with a resale house for the same buyers, and it can bring new streets, utilities and traffic. If your house is near open land, check the city's planning pages for pending applications before you set a timeline.

Deschutes County collects tax on Redmond homes. This year's due dates are November 16, February 16 and May 17. Here is what each choice earns.

Payment optionDue dateDiscount
Pay in fullNovember 163%
Pay two-thirdsNovember 162%
Three installmentsNovember 16, February 16, May 17None

Interest starts to accrue on December 16. Mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date, and metered postmarks from mail machines are not accepted. The property tax office is at 1300 NW Wall Street, Suite 203, in Bend, phone 541-388-6540, and a drop box in Redmond keeps limited hours. The Deschutes County payment page has current details.

Under Measure 50, assessed values generally cannot rise more than about 3 percent a year, so a Redmond house owned for many years may carry a low assessed value. The escrow company prorates the tax between buyer and seller at closing.

sections.h2: What a Redmond seller must disclose
sections.html:
Each buyer who makes a written offer gets a property disclosure statement from the seller, and the buyer has five days after delivery to revoke unless that right is waived. The form asks about title, water, sewage, structure, systems and general conditions.

ORS 105.470 excludes some sales, such as one by a court-appointed personal representative, trustee or guardian, or one by a financial institution after foreclosure. Those sellers complete only Section 1.

An as-is sale is allowed in Oregon, though you still give the buyer the disclosure statement unless an exclusion applies. A cash buyer prices the house in its present condition, so you do not need to repaint, replace a worn deck or fix a sprinkler zone first. Compare any offer by what you actually keep after closing costs, taxes and repairs the buyer wants you to handle.

1. Tell the buyer the address, the condition and when you want to close.
  2. Read the written offer for closing costs, as-is wording and the closing date.
  3. Escrow opens at a title company, which searches for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and your proceeds are paid.

Nobody needs lender approval, so the loan appraisal that often delays a financed sale is not part of this timeline.

Overdue tax is paid from your proceeds at closing, with interest. Ask the title company for a payoff figure early, or call the tax office at 541-388-6540 to see what the county shows. Knowing the number before you accept an offer prevents a surprise at the signing table.

• Photo ID that matches the deed.
  • The current tax statement.
  • Lender and loan number if there is a mortgage to pay off.
  • Papers for permits, roof work or sprinkler repairs.
  • Lease records if a tenant lives there.

Having these in hand keeps the closing date from slipping.

sections.h2: Getting a High Desert house ready to show
sections.html:
Buyers coming from wetter parts of the state notice dry-climate wear right away. Touch up sun-faded trim, seal cracked wood on a deck or fence, and make sure every hose bib and exposed pipe is in working order after the winter freezes. Turn the sprinklers on before a showing so a buyer can see the landscaping alive and the system running.

If you would rather not spend the money, a cash sale lets you hand over the house as it is. The offer will reflect the condition, and you skip the weeks of showings and inspection back-and-forth.

Because the airport draws visitors and newcomers, some of your buyers will be unfamiliar with Central Oregon. Be specific in the listing about distance to Bend, the lot, the heating and cooling, and the freeze protection on the plumbing. A buyer who understands the house is easier to close with.

faqs.q: How far is Redmond from Bend?
faqs.a: About 17 miles north. Bend is the Deschutes County seat, and Redmond sits at roughly 3,012 feet in the High Desert on the eastern side of the Cascades.

faqs.q: When are Redmond property taxes due?
faqs.a: Deschutes County's installments are due November 16, February 16 and May 17. A full payment by the first date earns a 3 percent discount, and two-thirds earns 2 percent.

faqs.q: What does the Redmond airport do for the local economy?
faqs.a: It is a hub for jobs and travel. Roberts Field has commercial service from four airlines, and the Redmond Air Center there is a U.S. Forest Service smokejumper and firefighting base.

faqs.q: Does wildfire risk affect selling a house in Redmond?
faqs.a: It can. Residents have raised fire access at a city council hearing, and buyers may ask the same questions. Answer the disclosure form questions honestly and ask your insurer what it needs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Redmond house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Oregon allows it, though you still give the buyer the disclosure statement unless an exclusion applies. A cash buyer prices the house in its present condition.
